remarks.name: Thibault Sottiaux
remarks.role: Codex & ChatGPT OpenAI
remarks.text:
Update on rate limits in Codex. 

We’ve found (a) some inefficiencies when using images in long sessions with multiple compactions (b) high p95+ usage for Computer History (c) a feature that was meant to generate conversation titles that was draining a bit more usage than intended. And we have a tiger team combing through everything and shipping fixes tomorrow. We also found a novel approach to drive efficiency up significantly that is completely unrelated and we will be working on next week.

As part of some of the fixes tomorrow, we will also do a full reset of the usage for all paid subscriptions.

See you then.
remarks.translation: 关于 Codex 中速率限制的更新。我们发现（a）在长时间会话中多次压缩时使用图像存在一些低效问题（b）Computer History 的 p95+ 使用量偏高（c）一个本应生成对话标题的功能消耗的使用量比预期略多。我们已组建一支攻坚团队，正在全面排查问题，并将于明天发布修复。我们还发现了一种全新的方法，可以显著提升效率，这与上述问题完全无关，我们将在下周着手处理。作为明天部分修复措施的一环，我们还将对所有付费订阅的使用量进行完全重置。届时见。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
AI diffusion is far more rate limited by having good evals than most realize. The kind of evals that you see for every model release are incredibly helpful, but only tell you the shape of general AI progress and the relative capability level of models.

The far bigger space over time are evals on all the major workflows that enterprises do, down to the specifics of an individual company. 

This will be a huge space over time because you can’t automate what you can’t assess the progress on. Enterprises will not be able to go just on vibes.
remarks.translation: AI扩散受限于优质评估的程度远超大多数人的认知。每次模型发布时所见的那种评估极为有用，但只能揭示通用AI进展的轮廓以及模型的相对能力水平。而随着时间的推移，更大的空间在于针对企业所有主要工作流程的评估，细化到单个公司的具体细节。这将是一个巨大的领域，因为无法评估进展的事物就无法自动化。企业不能仅凭感觉行事。

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text:
How to build great evals - part 6

Hill climbing on evals is just a fancy way of saying: pick a dimension that matters and optimize for it.

This could be improving the quality of existing features based on your latest production data on high value user journeys, expanding to adjacent use cases, lowering cost or latency.

The actual work boils down to better harnesses and model selection through methods like prompt eng, context eng, memory, post training, deterministic old school code etc.

Your failure mode taxonomy (from part 3) is a good compass for where your product struggles and needs some love.

E.g. maybe tool calling failures are your most common problem. You dig in and notice you stuff 20 tools in context, when each task really only needs 3-5. hill climbing here involves context eng to give it the right tools at the right stage and iterate until you get it to good.

Or take the cost reduction goal..
I’ve written about how I advise launching your product with the best model first. Get the quality as high as you can. Once you know users love the experience, hill climb to get similar quality with a smaller, cheaper, faster model. Same methods - harness, models.

The important thing is to have evals that tell you whether you are actually moving in the right direction.

More tomorrow. 

Send this to your teammates!

Drop your questions in the comments and I will answer in future posts.
remarks.translation:
如何构建出色的评估——第6部分

在评估上进行“爬山”只是一种花哨的说法：选择一个重要的维度，并针对它进行优化。这可以是根据你最新的生产数据，在高价值用户旅程上改进现有功能的质量，扩展到相邻的用例，降低成本和延迟。实际工作归结为更好的测试框架和模型选择，方法包括提示工程、上下文工程、记忆、后训练、确定性的传统代码等。你的失败模式分类法（来自第3部分）是一个很好的指南针，能告诉你产品在哪里遇到困难、需要改进。例如，也许工具调用失败是你最常见的问题。你深入研究后发现，你把20个工具塞进了上下文里，而每个任务实际上只需要3到5个。这里的爬山就涉及上下文工程，在正确的阶段给它正确的工具，并不断迭代，直到把它做好。或者以降低成本为目标……我写过我建议先用最好的模型来发布产品。把质量尽可能做高。一旦你知道用户喜欢这种体验，就通过爬山来用更小、更便宜、更快的模型达到类似的质量。方法是一样的——测试框架、模型。重要的是要有评估来告诉你，你是否真的在朝正确的方向前进。明天继续。把这个发给你的队友们！在评论区留下你的问题，我会在未来的帖子中回答。

podcasts.originalTitle: Microsoft’s Vision for an Internet Made for Agents With CTO Kevin Scott (Best of the Pod)
podcasts.excerpt: 2025年，凯文·斯科特押注智能体网络将成为人工智能领域的下一件大事。这位微软首席技术官认为，要让智能体真正有用，它们需要能够代表我们采取行动——这意味着要让它们访问构成互联网的同样庞杂的工具、数据和系统。如今，这一押注开始见效，因为智能体网络的基础设施正在建设中。在本周的AI & I节目中，丹·希珀重温了他与凯文的对话。他们讨论了微软在智能体网络中的角色、为什么开放性不必以牺牲安全性为代价，以及为什么程序员应该对新工具保持好奇，而不是出于原则而抵制它们。如果你觉得这期节目有趣，请点赞、订阅、评论并分享！想听更多丹·希珀的内容：订阅Every：https://…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: In 2025, Kevin Scott bet that the agentic web would be the next big thing in AI.The Microsoft CTO argued that for agents to be genuinely useful, they'd need to be able to take action on our behalf—which would mean giving them access to the same sprawl of tools, data, and systems that make up the internet. Today, that bet is starting to pay off, as the foundational infrastructure for the agentic web is now being built.On this week's AI & I, Dan Shipper revisits his conversation with Kevin. They discuss Microsoft's role in the agentic web, why openness doesn't have to come at the expense of security, and why programmers should stay curious about new tools rather than resist them on principle.If you found this episode interesting, please like, subscribe, comment, and share!To hear more from Dan Shipper:Subscribe to Every: https://…
